title: A Method for Evaluating Timeliness and Accuracy of Volitional Motor Responses to Vibrotactile Stimuli
protocol: Connect the microcontroller board to the computer using an USB port.
Upload the custom script "Motor_and_AccelerometerTest.ino" to the board via USB connection.
Set the vibration level to zero by specifying "analogWrite(vibe1,0);" in the code.
Initialize the PWM output pin corresponding to the motor of interest as "vibe1".
Connect the z-axis output of the tri-axis accelerometer to an analog input port on the microcontroller board.
Connect the positive and ground leads from the accelerometer to the 5V and GND ports of the microcontroller, respectively.
Mount the accelerometer to the vibrating motor with its z-axis orthogonal to the flat surface of the motor.
Open the "Motor_Calibration.vi" file in the data acquisition software.
Connect the microcontroller to the computer through an USB port.
Specify the serial port for the microcontroller input using the dropdown menu.
Set the sampling rate to 500 Hz.
Set the number of samples to collect to 1,000.
Use the "Motor_and_Accelerometer.ino" code to specify the desired duty cycle of the PWM pulses supplied to the vibratory motor.
Re-download the program to the microcontroller board controlling the motors.
Identify the largest peak using the FFT display on the "MotorCalibration.vi" interface.
Record the corresponding vibration frequency value from the horizontal axis.
Adjust the PWM levels until the desired frequency is reached.
Repeat Steps 1.7-1.8 with adjusted PWM levels to find the PWM-frequency pair for the target frequency.
Repeat Steps 1.2.2 to 1.8 for each motor, manually recording the PWM-frequency relationship for each motor with a spreadsheet or pencil and paper.
Open the "Experiment_1.vi" file.
Right-click on the dropdown frequency menu and select "Property".
Under the "Edit Items" tab, use the table to enter the desired frequencies and corresponding PWM levels determined in Steps 1.8-1.9.
Select "OK" to exit.
Repeat Step 1.11 for each virtual interface (VI) file of the system design software to be used during testing (e.g., "Experiment_2.vi", "Experiment_3.vi", etc.).
Place one motor on each of the anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral surfaces of the thigh.
Position motors approximately midway between the greater trochanter and lateral femoral condyle.
Attach motors directly to the skin using double-sided tape.
Optionally shave the region around each motor to improve adhesion.
For applications involving clothing or prosthetic liners, place motors on top of these materials rather than against the skin.
Re-flash the microcontroller board with firmware using "LVIFA_Base.pde" file.
Connect the push-button to a USB port via a serial-to-USB connector.
Install all required drivers on the computer.
Open the "Experiment_1.vi" interface.
Select the serial ports for the microcontroller board and push-button from dropdown menus labeled "Motor Input" and "Green Button".
Identify serial port identification numbers using device manager utility.
Select the file to record results in the data acquisition software.
Start the program by selecting motors and frequencies from dropdown menus.
Have the participant press the push-button upon feeling a vibration.
Confirm response in the data acquisition software when clock stops counting.
Reset the motors for the next trial by selecting new frequencies from dropdown menus.
Use the dropdown menus to return all motor frequencies to the zero position.
Select the "Stop Program" button to terminate the connection to the motor control board.
Connect a second push-button to another USB port using a serial-USB connector.
Open the "Experiment_2.vi" data acquisition interface.
Place motors in locations and configurations required for the specific research application.
Specify the serial ports for the microcontroller board and both push-buttons as per Step 3.4.
Note which push-button is assigned to each port.
Select specific motors and desired sequence of frequencies using the software interface.
Input a delayed start time of 1.5 seconds.
Input a stimulation duration of 1.5 seconds.
Start the program.
Have the participant press one of two push-buttons after each vibration sequence to indicate if the second frequency was higher or lower than the first.
